text:
Predicates:
Fights(x, y) ::: x fights y.
Wins(x, y) ::: x wins y.
Loses(x, y) ::: x loses y.
NameAfter(x, y) ::: x is named after y.
AppearsIn(x, y) ::: x appears in y.
GoodGuys(x) ::: x are good guys.
BadGuys(x) ::: x are bad guys.
Movie(y) ::: y is a movie.
Character(y) ::: y is a character.
SuperheroMovie(y) ::: y is a superhero movie.
Fights(x, y) ::: x fights y.
Nemesis(x, y) ::: x is nemesis of y.
Name(y, z) ::: y is named after z.

Premises:
The Surprising Adventures of Sir Digby Chicken Caesar is a superhero movie.
SuperheroMovie(theMovie) ::: The Surprising Adventures of Sir Digby Chicken Caesar is a superhero movie.
NameAfter(theMovie, SirDigby) ::: The Surprising Adventures of Sir Digby Chicken Caesar is named after Sir Digby.
Fights(SirDigby, nemesis) ::: Sir Digby fights his nemesis.
If a superhero movie is named after a character, that character is a good guy.
∀y (NameAfter(y, x) ∧ SuperheroMovie(y) → GoodGuys(x)) ::: If a superhero movie is named after a character, that character is a good guy.
SirDigby is a character.
AppearsIn(SirDigby, theMovie) ::: Sir Digby appears in the movie.
If somebody wins a fight, the person they are fighting loses.
∀x, y, z (Wins(x, y) ∧ Fights(x, y) → Loses(y, x)) ::: If someone wins a fight, the opponent loses.
SirDigby fights his nemesis.
The premise is repeated.

Conclusion:
Loses(nemesis, SirDigby) ::: Sir Digby’s nemesis loses.
